title: September 2026 arXiv physics: the month’s most visible results
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred visibility/significance ranking, and citation evidence is sparse for papers this new.

sections.title: Search for dark matter particle interactions in an extended nuclear recoil energy window with the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment
sections.abstract: The LZ Collaboration extends its xenon nuclear-recoil search to higher energies and reports one 248-keV recoil-like event in 2.84 tonne-years of exposure.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The collaboration's result was announced by LZ and covered by Brown University; the unusual event also prompted a cluster of September dark-matter interpretation papers, including the boosted-dark-matter proposal ranked below.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a recoil candidate at 248 ± 23(stat) ± 23(sys) keV; their background-only test gives 2.6σ global significance after look-elsewhere effects (3.4σ maximum local).
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; 2.84 tonne-year LZ exposure, using an extended nuclear-recoil window up to about 270 keV.
sections.unique_caveat: This is one event, not a dark-matter detection. The collaboration says the result does not meet the discovery threshold and needs more data.

sections.title: In-orbit operation of a programmable quantum photonic processor
sections.abstract: The team reports a programmable photonic platform on a nanosatellite, processing two photons in a six-mode integrated circuit and observing two-photon interference in orbit.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The in-orbit demonstration received independent quantum-industry coverage, and the paper describes programmable processing with interference rather than only photon generation or transmission.
sections.claimed_result: The authors demonstrate on-board generation, manipulation and detection of non-classical light by programming unitaries and making the photons indistinguishable.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; a nanosatellite payload with a six-mode universal photonic integrated circuit, photon-pair source and single-photon detectors.
sections.unique_caveat: This establishes an in-orbit processing primitive, not a useful end-to-end quantum computation or a demonstrated quantum advantage.

sections.title: Magnetic-field-induced Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and Bose-Einstein condensate phases in an organic S=1 Haldane chain
sections.abstract: A high-field NMR study of the organic Haldane-chain material BoNO maps field-induced Tomonaga-Luttinger-liquid and Bose-Einstein-condensate phases, with quantum Monte Carlo and other calculations used to interpret the phase boundary.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The revised preprint was featured by APS Physics on the same date and is published in Physical Review Letters; the paper combines measurements with numerical approaches.
sections.claimed_result: The authors use proton NMR up to 34 T to map the phase boundary, report a critical exponent of 2/3 near the upper critical field, and infer attractive interactions within the liquid phase.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental and computational; low-temperature 1H NMR and pulsed-field magnetostriction, interpreted with quantum Monte Carlo and density-matrix renormalization group calculations.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is specific to BoNO; the phase diagram and interaction inference do not by themselves establish the same behavior in other Haldane-chain materials.

sections.title: Euclid: Data Release 1 (DR1) – Fornax-7, an ultra-faint companion to the Fornax dwarf spheroidal galaxy?
sections.abstract: Using Euclid DR1 and ground-based photometry, the authors identify Fornax-7, an exceptionally low-mass stellar system near the Fornax dwarf spheroidal galaxy, and assess possible classifications.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The candidate received independent science-news coverage; its low inferred stellar mass and possible satellite-of-a-satellite interpretation make it a distinctive Euclid DR1 result.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer a stellar mass of 170 (+50/−62) solar masses and a distance consistent with Fornax under their low-metallicity assumption; possibilities include a remote cluster, a Fornax satellite, or an independent Milky Way satellite.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; Euclid DR1 imaging plus ground-based colour-magnitude, luminosity-function and integrated-colour data analyzed through forward modelling.
sections.unique_caveat: Its nature and dynamical association remain unresolved; inferred properties depend partly on metallicity assumptions, and the authors call for deeper photometry and spectroscopy.

sections.title: Measurement of Neutrino Oscillation Parameters at JUNO and Indication of the Neutrino Mass Ordering
sections.abstract: JUNO reports improved reactor-neutrino oscillation measurements from its first 207.2 live days and an indication favoring normal mass ordering when combined with accelerator-neutrino constraints.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A new result from a major underground neutrino experiment, based on a substantial first dataset, provides a timely precision measurement; the mass-ordering inference links reactor and accelerator data.
sections.claimed_result: The collaboration reports about 1% precision on the atmospheric mass splitting and improved solar parameters; adding long-baseline accelerator constraints favors normal ordering at at least 2.1σ across CP phases.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; 8,294 inverse-beta-decay candidates collected over 207.2 live days at an average reactor baseline of 52.5 km.
sections.unique_caveat: The ordering is an indication, not a discovery; the ≥2.1σ preference incorporates external long-baseline constraints.

sections.title: MAGGIE: A Magnetic Gravitational Wave Induction Experiment
sections.abstract: MAGGIE is a proposed high-frequency gravitational-wave detector using GW-induced electromagnetic currents in a 14 T solenoidal magnet and a purpose-built pickup-loop readout.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The proposal cross-lists four physics areas and turns a high-frequency gravitational-wave coupling into a concrete detector design using an existing 14 T magnet; its reach is projected, not measured.
sections.claimed_result: The authors project sensitivity to currently unexplored high-frequency parameter space, including strain near 10^-19 for a one-year continuous search.
sections.evidence_type: Forecast/proposal; design and sensitivity projections for a magnet-and-pickup-loop experiment, with transient templates including primordial-black-hole mergers.
sections.unique_caveat: No gravitational-wave signal or detector performance is reported; projected sensitivity depends on eventual instrument noise and implementation.

sections.title: High-Energy Nuclear Recoils from Boosted Dark Matter for the LZ 248-keV Event: Beyond the Halo-Dependent High-Velocity Tail
sections.abstract: This theoretical paper proposes light, boosted dark matter as one possible explanation for the LZ high-energy recoil, with benchmark spectra designed to suppress events outside the candidate's energy region.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It is a directly testable theoretical response to the month’s most visible dark-matter result; the authors propose complementary checks with other targets and liquid-scintillator experiments, but it is a model interpretation rather than independent evidence.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show representative multi-component boosted-dark-matter scenarios that can confine recoil signals through momentum dependence or kinematic endpoints.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; benchmark dark-sector spectra and scattering models compared with the LZ event and recoil sidebands.
sections.unique_caveat: The proposal explains one candidate under selected model assumptions; it neither establishes dark matter nor resolves the event’s origin.
